university: University of Arkansas at Little Rock

documents.unit: Office of the Executive Vice Chancellor and Provost
documents.title: Resources for Faculty on Student Use of AI
documents.summary: Provost guidance for faculty on student AI use. It asks instructors to state and discuss their own AI policy, lists signs and tools for detecting AI use, and outlines talking to the student and reporting to an integrity office.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no AI rule of its own; it tells faculty to "explicitly state your policies on AI tools" in the syllabus and gives detection and reporting guidance, leaving permissibility to each instructor.

units.why: Lists a tool for finding AI text: "provides AI-generated content detection". Detector use to identify misuse fits P40 (tools used to identify misuse), addressed to faculty at the point of suspicion.
units.anchor: A tool that not only checks grammar but also provides AI-generated content detection

units.why: Faculty are told to "explicitly state your policies on AI tools" at course start; this is a duty to communicate expectations, so P09 (statement in the syllabus/course) rather than P04, since the rule is about stating, not about who decides.
units.anchor: At the beginning of each course, explicitly state your policies on AI tools

units.why: "Include these guidelines in your syllabus" directs instructors to put AI rules in the syllabus; P09 fits exactly. The in-class discussion half of the sentence is coded separately as P66.
units.anchor: Include these guidelines in your syllabus
units.policy: Include the AI policy guidelines in the syllabus.

units.why: "discuss them in class to emphasize their importance" asks instructors to talk through the rules with students beyond listing them, which is P66 (explain and discuss the rules).
units.anchor: discuss them in class to emphasize their importance

units.why: "specific examples of acceptable and unacceptable uses of AI" is advice to illustrate the rules for students; P66 fits (going beyond listing the rule) better than P05, which needs named tiers.
units.anchor: providing specific examples of acceptable and unacceptable uses of AI

units.why: Gives the reason for clear expectations: "crucial for maintaining academic integrity". The rationale is integrity, not skill-building, so P95 rather than P41.
units.anchor: crucial for maintaining academic integrity

units.why: Names indicators of AI use to weigh, such as "unusual consistency in tone or style". This is guidance on the kinds of evidence to look for, which P69 covers; P40 is for tools and logs.
units.anchor: Look for unusual consistency in tone or style
units.fit_note: States the kinds of evidence to weigh (style, generic phrasing, unexplained errors) but no standard of proof.

units.why: Admits that "Detecting the use of AI in student work can be challenging", acknowledging limits on verification, which is P82.
units.anchor: Detecting the use of AI in student work can be challenging

units.why: Says Turnitin AI-detection "can flag sections of text likely to have been generated by AI"; detection tools used to identify misuse is P40.
units.anchor: Turnitin now offer AI-detection features that can flag sections of text

units.why: "use these tools as part of a broader assessment rather than relying on them exclusively" makes detector output supporting evidence only, covered by P69 as broadened; not P39 because detectors are still used.
units.anchor: use these tools as part of a broader assessment rather than relying on them exclusively

units.why: "Begin by discussing your concerns with the student" tells instructors to talk to the student first, P57 exactly.
units.anchor: Begin by discussing your concerns with the student

units.why: "giving them an opportunity to explain their process and intentions" lets the student respond to the suspicion, P64.
units.anchor: giving them an opportunity to explain their process and intentions

units.why: "report the incident to the appropriate academic integrity office or committee, providing documentation" is a procedural step after suspected misuse, P81.
units.anchor: report the incident to the appropriate academic integrity office or committee

units.why: "clearly explain how the student’s use of AI violated your course policies" adds a content requirement to the report; it is part of the formal reporting procedure, P81, and implies the violation is measured against the course policy.
units.anchor: clearly explain how the student’s use of AI violated your course policies

units.why: "follow your institution’s procedures for addressing academic integrity violations" treats improper AI use as an integrity violation handled by existing procedures, P36.
units.anchor: follow your institution’s procedures for addressing academic integrity violations

units.why: "Maintaining transparency and fairness throughout this process is essential" sets fairness and transparency in AI integrity cases, P64.
units.anchor: Maintaining transparency and fairness throughout this process is essential

units.why: States the purpose of the page: support faculty so "students and instructors can leverage these technologies responsibly and effectively". A scope and purpose statement, P56.
units.anchor: support faculty in navigating the complex landscape of AI and LLMs in academia

documents.unit: Office of the Executive Vice Chancellor and Provost
documents.title: Purpose Statement on Artificial Intelligence
documents.summary: A short framework statement saying AI offers opportunities for learning, research and administration alongside privacy, bias and misuse risks. It lists goals for ethical use, AI literacy and DEI but gives no operational rules.
documents.stance_why: The statement sets goals rather than rules and welcomes AI: "Promote the ethical and effective use of AI in teaching, research, and administration" and "Encourage the development of AI literacy".

units.why: "establish a comprehensive framework for the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence" states purpose and scope for faculty, staff and students: P56.
units.anchor: establish a comprehensive framework for the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence

units.why: Names a benefit: AI "can enhance learning experiences through personalized education". A benefit claim, not a rule: P87.
units.anchor: enhance learning experiences through personalized education

units.why: Says AI integration aims at "preparing our community for future careers", a career-skill argument for AI use: P44.
units.anchor: preparing our community for future careers and societal contributions

units.why: Names "data privacy, algorithmic bias, and the potential for misuse" as issues needing "proactive management"; concerns about harms, P53, though privacy is also touched.
units.anchor: Issues such as data privacy, algorithmic bias, and the potential for misuse

units.why: "ensure that AI applications align with our core values of equity, transparency, and accountability" is a principle for the institution-level framework: P56.
units.anchor: align with our core values of equity, transparency, and accountability

units.why: "Promote the ethical and effective use of AI in teaching, research, and administration" welcomes AI use within an ethical frame; closest is P56 (principles), but it also promotes use, hence the note.
units.anchor: Promote the ethical and effective use of AI in teaching, research, and administration
units.fit_note: Also expresses a positive stance toward AI use, which P56 does not capture.

units.why: "Encourage the development of AI literacy and skills among all members" is a commitment to AI literacy for the whole community: P70.
units.anchor: Encourage the development of AI literacy and skills among all members

units.why: "upholds our commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion" requires AI deployment to respect DEI commitments; no type covers AI deployment tied to DEI (P51 is about cost and access).
units.anchor: deployed in a manner that upholds our commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion
units.frag_start: Ensure that AI technologies are deployed
units.uncovered_note: AI technologies must be deployed in a way that upholds the university’s commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion.

units.why: "Foster interdisciplinary collaboration in AI research and application" is a goal for research collaboration; not a rule about teaching AI use, and P88 is for external partners, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Foster interdisciplinary collaboration in AI research and application
units.uncovered_note: The university aims to foster interdisciplinary collaboration in AI research and application.

units.why: "Provide a framework for addressing ethical, legal, and societal implications of AI" states a goal of framing ethics and legal issues: P53 is closest (names harms), but this is a framework aim.
units.anchor: Provide a framework for addressing ethical, legal, and societal implications of AI
units.fit_note: States an aim to provide a framework for ethical, legal and societal implications rather than naming specific harms.

documents.unit: Office of the Executive Vice Chancellor and Provost
documents.title: Resources for Students on Use of AI
documents.summary: A thin page of student links: an ethics course, Grammarly, Purdue citation guidance. It tells students to check each syllabus and ask instructors when unsure.
documents.stance_why: The page issues no AI rule; it sends students to their syllabus ("Review your syllabus carefully") and instructors ("reach out to your professor") for course-specific AI policy.

units.why: Points students to a free ethics course, "Kaggle: Intro to Ethics Free Online Course with Certificate of Completion", i.e. AI-literacy training for students: P70.
units.anchor: Kaggle: Intro to Ethics Free Online Course with Certificate of Completion

units.why: Recommends Grammarly for "plagiarism checking and alerts for potential AI-generated content" so students self-check originality; closest is P40 (similarity checks), but here students use it on their own work.
units.anchor: plagiarism checking and alerts for potential AI-generated content
units.fit_note: A self-check aid offered to students rather than a tool used by staff to identify misuse.

units.why: Links "Purdue Information on Citing AI", pointing students to guidance on citing AI use; no rule is stated, so P24 fits partly.
units.anchor: Purdue Information on Citing AI
units.fit_note: Only a link to external citation guidance; no requirement to cite is stated on this page.

units.why: "Review your syllabus carefully for any specific guidelines your instructors have set regarding AI use" makes students responsible for finding the course rules: P78.
units.anchor: Review your syllabus carefully for any specific guidelines your instructors have set regarding AI use

units.why: "restrictions on AI assistance or requirements for disclosing AI contributions" shows that instructors may set restrictions or disclosure, i.e. a course-level decision; P04.
units.anchor: restrictions on AI assistance or requirements for disclosing AI contributions

units.why: "If you’re unsure about how to use AI tools in a course, reach out to your professor" is ask-first advice: P10.
units.anchor: reach out to your professor for clarification and guidance

documents.title: LR 501.13 Academic Offenses (academic integrity and grievance)
documents.summary: Board-approved academic offenses policy. Only two sentences concern AI: unauthorized generative AI counts as cheating and unacknowledged generative AI counts as plagiarism.
documents.stance_why: Unauthorized AI is misconduct: "Using unauthorized notes or materials (including any form of generative AI)" is cheating, and unacknowledged generative AI is plagiarism, so AI is banned unless authorized or acknowledged.

units.why: Lists "Using unauthorized notes or materials (including any form of generative AI)" as cheating, so unauthorized generative AI is academic misconduct: P36. Banned unless authorized.
units.anchor: Using unauthorized notes or materials (including any form of generative AI)

units.why: Defines plagiarism as including "using ideas, words, or products produced by any form of Generative AI without proper acknowledgement". Chose P28 (nondisclosure is the violation) over P36 because the distinguishing rule is that unacknowledged AI use is the offense, implying acknowledged use is not.
units.anchor: products produced by any form of Generative AI without proper acknowledgement

documents.title: LR 404.8 Course Syllabus
documents.summary: Faculty Senate syllabus policy, revised February 2, 2026. Among the required syllabus elements, it includes the instructor’s own statement on whether students may use generative AI.
documents.stance_why: The policy only requires a syllabus statement on "the permissibility of student use of generative AI", leaving the actual rule to the instructor.

units.why: Requires every syllabus to carry "The instructor’s statement on the permissibility of student use of generative AI". A mandatory syllabus element: P09; it also leaves the permissibility to instructors (P04) but P09 is the operative rule.
units.anchor: statement on the permissibility of student use of generative AI
units.frag_start: The instructor’s statement on the permissibility
units.fit_note: Also delegates the AI decision to the instructor (P04).
